body.translated_text: <s>Mahādaṇḍadhāraṇīśītavatī</s> (The Great Dhāraṇī of the Staff of the Cool-Forest)

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma | śītavane mahāśmaśāne iṅghikāyatanapratyuddeśe | tatrāyuṣmān rāhulo 'tīva viheṭhyate devagrahair nāgagrahair yakṣagrahai rākṣasagrahaiḥ kinnaragrahair garuḍagrahair mahoragagrahair manuṣyagrahair amanuṣyagrahaiḥ pretagrahair bhūtagrahaiḥ piśācagrahaiḥ kumbhāṇḍagrahair dvīpibhiḥ kākair ulūkaiḥ kīṭaiḥ sarīsṛpaiṛ anyaiś ca manuṣyāmanuṣyaiḥ sattvaiḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Śītavana</s> (Cool Forest), the great charnel ground, at the site of the charnel ground entrance. There, the venerable <s>Rāhula</s> was being greatly afflicted by possessing spirits of gods (<s>devagrahaiḥ</s>), nāgas (<s>nāgagrahaiḥ</s>), <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, great serpents (<s>mahoragaiḥ</s>), humans, non-humans, ghosts (<s>pretaiḥ</s>), spirits (<s>bhūtaiḥ</s>), <s>piśācas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, leopards, crows, owls, insects, reptiles, and other human and non-human beings.

body.text: athāyuṣmān rāhulo yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivanditvā bhagavantaṃ tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ purato rudann aśrūṇi pravartayati sma |
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Rāhula</s> approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage with his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and stood weeping before the Blessed One, shedding tears.

body.text: atha bhagavān jānann eva rāhulam āmantrayate sma | kiṃ tvaṃ rāhula mama purataḥ sthitvā aśrūṇi pravartayasi | evam ukte āyuṣmān rāhulo bhagavantam etad avocat | ihāhaṃ bhagavan rājagṛhe viharāmi | śītavane mahāśmaśāne iṅghikāyatanapratyuddeśe | so 'haṃ bhagavaṃs tatra viheṭhye devagrahair nāgagrahair yakṣagrahai rākṣasagrahaiḥ kinnaragrahair garuḍagrahair mahoragagrahair manuṣyagrahair amanuṣyagrahaiḥ pretagrahair bhūtagrahaiḥ piśācagrahaiḥ kumbhāṇḍagrahair dvīpibhiḥ kākair ulūkaiḥ kīṭaiḥ sarīsṛpair anyaiś ca manuṣyāmanuṣyaiḥ sattvair iti |
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, already knowing, addressed <s>Rāhula</s>: "Why do you stand before me shedding tears?" When this was said, the venerable <s>Rāhula</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Here, Blessed One, I am dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Śītavana</s>, the great charnel ground, at the site of the charnel ground entrance. I, Blessed One, am being afflicted there by possessing spirits of gods, nāgas, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, great serpents, humans, non-humans, ghosts, spirits, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, leopards, crows, owls, insects, reptiles, and other human and non-human beings."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ rāhulam āmantrayate sma | udgṛhṇa tvaṃ rāhula imāṃ mahādaṇḍadhāraṇīṃ vidyām | catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptaye bhikṣūṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīnām upāsakānām upāsikānāṃ ca dīrgharātram arthāya hitāya sukhāya bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Rāhula</s>: "Learn, O <s>Rāhula</s>, this <s>mahādaṇḍadhāraṇī</s> (great staff dhāraṇī) vidyā. For the protection, guarding, and safeguarding of the four assemblies — monks (<s>bhikṣus</s>), nuns (<s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>), laymen (<s>upāsakas</s>), and laywomen (<s>upāsikās</s>) — it will be for long-lasting benefit, welfare, and happiness."

body.text: tadyathā | aṅgā | vaṅgā | bhaṅgā | varaṅgā | saṃsārataraṅgā | sāsadaṅgā | bhaṅgā | jesurā | ekatarā | ara vīrā | tara vīrā | kara vīrā | kara kara vīrā | indrā | indrakisarā | haṃsā | haṃsakisarā | picimalā | mahākiccā | viheṭhikā | kālucchikā | aṅgodarā | jayā | jayālikā | velā | elā | cintāli | cili cili | hili hili | sumati | vasumati | culu naṭṭe | culu culu naṭṭe | culu nāḍi | kunāḍi | hārīṭaki | kārīṭaki | gauri | gandhāri | caṇḍāli | mātaṅgi | dharaṇi dhāraṇi | uṣṭrapālike | kaca kārike | cala nāṭike | kākalike | lalamati | rakṣamati | varākule | manmate utpale | kara vīre | tara vīre | tara tara vīre | kuru vīre | kuru kuru vīre | curu vīre | curu curu vīre | mahāvīre | iramati | varamati | rakṣamati | sarvārthasādhani | paramārthasādhani | apratihate | indro rājā | yamo rājā | varuṇo rājā | kubero rājā | manasvī rājā | vāsukī rājā | daṇḍāgnī rājā | brahmā sahasrādhipatī rājā | buddho bhagavān dharmasvāmī rājā | anuttaro lokānukampakaḥ | mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ kurvantu | paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca kurvantu | jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāṃ śatam |
body.translated_text: Thus: <s>Aṅgā | Vaṅgā | Bhaṅgā | Varaṅgā | Saṃsārataraṅgā | Sāsadaṅgā | Bhaṅgā | Jesurā | Ekatarā | Ara Vīrā | Tara Vīrā | Kara Vīrā | Kara Kara Vīrā | Indrā | Indrakisarā | Haṃsā | Haṃsakisarā | Picimalā | Mahākiccā | Viheṭhikā | Kālucchikā | Aṅgodarā | Jayā | Jayālikā | Velā | Elā | Cintāli | Cili Cili | Hili Hili | Sumati | Vasumati | Culu Naṭṭe | Culu Culu Naṭṭe | Culu Nāḍi | Kunāḍi | Hārīṭaki | Kārīṭaki | Gauri | Gandhāri | Caṇḍāli | Mātaṅgi | Dharaṇi Dhāraṇi | Uṣṭrapālike | Kaca Kārike | Cala Nāṭike | Kākalike | Lalamati | Rakṣamati | Varākule | Manmate Utpale | Kara Vīre | Tara Vīre | Tara Tara Vīre | Kuru Vīre | Kuru Kuru Vīre | Curu Vīre | Curu Curu Vīre | Mahāvīre | Iramati | Varamati | Rakṣamati | Sarvārthasādhani | Paramārthasādhani | Apratihate</s> — may <s>Indra</s>, the king; <s>Yama</s>, the king; <s>Varuṇa</s>, the king; <s>Kubera</s>, the king; <s>Manasvī</s>, the king; <s>Vāsukī</s>, the king; <s>Daṇḍāgni</s>, the king; <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of a thousand, the king; the Blessed Buddha, lord of the <s>Dharma</s>, the king; the unsurpassed one compassionate toward the world — may they perform protection (<s>rakṣā</s>), rescue (<s>paritrāṇa</s>), safeguarding (<s>parigraha</s>), guarding (<s>paripālana</s>), peace (<s>śānti</s>), benediction (<s>svastyayana</s>), warding off of clubs (<s>daṇḍaparihāra</s>), warding off of weapons (<s>śastraparihāra</s>), dispelling of poison (<s>viṣadūṣaṇa</s>), destruction of poison (<s>viṣanāśana</s>), binding of boundaries (<s>sīmābandha</s>), and binding of the earth (<s>dharaṇībandha</s>) for me and all sentient beings. May [the recipient] live a hundred years; may [they] see a hundred autumns.

body.text: tadyathā | balavati | varamati | talamati | lakṣamati | rakṣamati | huru huru | phuru phuru | cara cara | khara khara | khuru khuru | mati mati | bhūmicaṇḍe | kālikeṭi | akisalā | pīne | sāmalate | hūle sthūle | sthūlaśikhare | jaya sthūle | jaya naṭṭe | cala nāsi | culu nāsi | vāgbandhani | virohaṇi | solohite | aṇḍare | paṇḍare | karāle | kinnare | keyūre | ketumati | bhūtaṃgame | bhūtamati | dhanye | maṅgalye | mahābalalohitamūle | acalacaṇḍe | dhuraṃdharā | jayālike | jayā | gorohaṇi | curu curu | rundha rundha | dhuru dhuru | khuru khuru | khurumati | bandhumati | dhuraṃdhare | dhare dhare | vidhare vimati | viṣkambhaṇi | nāśani vināśani | bandhani | mokṣaṇi | mocani | mohani | bhāvani | śodhani | saṃśodhani viśodhani | saṃkhiraṇi | saṃchindani | sādhu turumāṇe | hara hara bandhumati | hiri hiri | khiri khiri | kharali | huru huru | piṅgale | namo 'stu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ svāhā |
body.translated_text: It is as follows: <s>Balavati</s>! <s>Varamati</s>! <s>Talamati</s>! <s>Lakṣamati</s>! <s>Rakṣamati</s>! <s>Huru huru</s>! <s>Phuru phuru</s>! <s>Cara cara</s>! <s>Khara khara</s>! <s>Khuru khuru</s>! <s>Mati mati</s>! <s>Bhūmicaṇḍe</s>! <s>Kālikeṭi</s>! <s>Akisalā</s>! <s>Pīne</s>! <s>Sāmalate</s>! <s>Hūle sthūle</s>! <s>Sthūlaśikhare</s>! <s>Jaya sthūle</s>! <s>Jaya naṭṭe</s>! <s>Cala nāsi</s>! <s>Culu nāsi</s>! <s>Vāgbandhani</s> (O binder of speech)! <s>Virohaṇi</s> (O one who sprouts forth)! <s>Solohite</s>! <s>Aṇḍare</s>! <s>Paṇḍare</s>! <s>Karāle</s> (O terrifying one)! <s>Kinnare</s>! <s>Keyūre</s> (O armlet)! <s>Ketumati</s> (O bannered one)! <s>Bhūtaṃgame</s>! <s>Bhūtamati</s>! <s>Dhanye</s> (O blessed one)! <s>Maṅgalye</s> (O auspicious one)! <s>Mahābalalohitamūle</s> (O one rooted in great power and blood)! <s>Acalacaṇḍe</s> (O fierce immovable one)! <s>Dhuraṃdharā</s> (O bearer of burdens)! <s>Jayālike</s>! <s>Jayā</s> (O victorious one)! <s>Gorohaṇi</s>! <s>Curu curu</s>! <s>Rundha rundha</s> (Obstruct, obstruct)! <s>Dhuru dhuru</s>! <s>Khuru khuru</s>! <s>Khurumati</s>! <s>Bandhumati</s> (O one rich in kinship)! <s>Dhuraṃdhare</s>! <s>Dhare dhare</s> (Hold, hold)! <s>Vidhare vimati</s>! <s>Viṣkambhaṇi</s> (O one who paralyzes)! <s>Nāśani vināśani</s> (O destroyer, O annihilator)! <s>Bandhani</s> (O binder)! <s>Mokṣaṇi</s> (O liberator)! <s>Mocani</s> (O releaser)! <s>Mohani</s> (O bewilderer)! <s>Bhāvani</s> (O cultivator)! <s>Śodhani</s> (O purifier)! <s>Saṃśodhani viśodhani</s> (O thorough purifier, O complete purifier)! <s>Saṃkhiraṇi</s>! <s>Saṃchindani</s> (O cutter)! <s>Sādhu turumāṇe</s>! <s>Hara hara bandhumati</s>! <s>Hiri hiri</s>! <s>Khiri khiri</s>! <s>Kharali</s>! <s>Huru huru</s>! <s>Piṅgale</s> (O tawny one)! Homage to the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text:
asyāṃ khalu rāhula mahādaṇḍadhāraṇyāṃ vidyāyām antaśo 'ṣṭottaraśatapadānāṃ sūtraṃ granthiṃ baddhāyāṃ hastena dhāryamāṇāyāṃ kaṇṭhena dhāryamāṇāyāṃ samantād yojanaśatasya rakṣā kṛtā bhaviṣyati | gandhair vā puṣpair vā mudrābhir vā naiva manuṣyo vāmanuṣyo vābhibhaviṣyati | na viṣaṃ na śastraṃ na rogo na jvaro na prajvaro na vidyāmantro na vetāḍaḥ | na vyādhau nāgnau na viṣodakena kālaṃ kariṣyati | vidyāmantraprayogānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ sādhuprayuktānāṃ ca bandhanī | parabandhānāṃ ca pramocanī | sarvarogaśokavighnavināśanakarī | kalikaluṣapraśamanakarī | sarvagrahavimocanakarī | yo graho na muñcet
saptadhāsya sphuṭen mūrdhā arjakasyeva mañjarī |
vajrapāṇiś cāsya mahāyakṣasenāpatir vajreṇādīptena samprajvālitena ekajvālībhūtena dhyāyitvā mūrdhānaṃ sphoṭayet | catvāraś ca mahārājāno 'yomayena cakreṇa kṣuradhārāprahāreṇa vināśayeyuḥ | tasmād yakṣalokāc cyavanaṃ bhavet | aḍakavatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ na labhate vāsam |
body.translated_text:
Now, O <s>Rāhula</s>, when a thread with a knot of one hundred and eight syllables of this great <s>Mahādaṇḍadhāraṇī</s> <s>vidyā</s> (spell) is held in the hand or worn around the neck, protection will be established for a hundred <s>yojanas</s> in every direction. Through incense, flowers, or <s>mudrās</s> (sacred gestures), neither a human nor a non-human being will be able to overpower (the bearer). Neither poison, nor weapons, nor disease, nor fever, nor burning fever, nor <s>vidyā-mantras</s> (hostile spells), nor a <s>vetāḍa</s> (zombie-spirit) — one will not die from illness, fire, or poisoned water. It binds all hostile <s>vidyā-mantra</s> applications and all well-employed (spells). It releases from the bonds of others. It destroys all diseases, sorrows, and obstacles. It pacifies the defilements of the <s>Kali</s> (dark age). It liberates from all <s>graha</s> (malign seizures). If a <s>graha</s> (seizing spirit) does not release (the victim),
his head will split sevenfold like the flower-cluster of the <s>arjaka</s> (basil) plant!
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Yakṣa</s> general, having meditated with his blazing, ignited <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) becoming a single flame, will split (the spirit's) head. And the four great kings will destroy (it) with an iron wheel delivering razor-sharp blows. There would be a falling from the <s>Yakṣa</s> realm, and it would not obtain residence in <s>Aḍakavatī</s>, the royal capital.

body.text: asyāṃ khalu rāhula mahādaṇḍadhāraṇyāṃ vidyāyāṃ sakṛtparivartitāyāṃ rājacaurodakāgniviṣaśastrāṭavīkāntāraparvatadurgamadhyagataḥ sarvabhayebhyaḥ pratimucyate | iyaṃ khalu mahādaṇḍadhāraṇīvidyā ekanavatigaṅgānadīvālikāsamair buddhair bhāṣitā bhāṣyate bhāṣiṣyate ca siddhā paramasiddhā sarvadevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhir vanditā sarvajanagaṇaparivṛtā | sarvabhayopadraveṣu mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca śivam ārogyaṃ bhavatu |
body.translated_text: Now, O <s>Rāhula</s>, when this great <s>Mahādaṇḍadhāraṇī vidyā</s> (spell) has been recited even once, one who finds himself amid dangers from kings, thieves, water, fire, poison, weapons, wilderness, desolate roads, or mountain fastnesses is freed from all fears. This great <s>Mahādaṇḍadhāraṇī vidyā</s> has been spoken, is being spoken, and will be spoken by <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as the grains of sand in ninety-one <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers. It is accomplished, supremely accomplished, venerated by all <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent beings), <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>, surrounded by all people. May there be welfare and health for me and for all beings amid all fears and calamities!

body.text: idam avocad bhagavān āttamanā āyuṣmān rāhulo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti |
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. The venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, with a joyful mind, rejoiced in the words spoken by the Blessed One.
The noble <s>Mahādaṇḍadhāraṇī Śītavatī</s> (The Great Staff Dhāraṇī, "The Cool One") is completed.
